lines: Taylor Nguyen
+1 (555) 010-6642 | taylor.nguyen@example.com | example.com/code/tnguyen
EDUCATION
Westfield State University | M.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Westfield State University | B.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2019 - Jun 2023
EXPERIENCE
Harbor Coffee Roasters | Barista | Metro City, USA | Oct 2025 - Present
- Prepared drinks for the morning rush of about 200 orders and kept the bar stocked.
- Opened the café three days a week and handled the daily cash count.
Lumen Travel | Frontend Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Sep 2025
- Improved page performance by 35% by code-splitting the calendar and map widgets.
- Added keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels to the date picker, fixing all 14 accessibility issues flagged in the audit.
- Wrote 60 component tests for the search filters, which caught 3 regressions before release.
- Cut the landing page's largest contentful paint from 4.1s to 1.2s by adding loading="lazy" to the hero image.
- Prevented cross-site scripting in comments by storing user input in React state before rendering it with dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
- Rebuilt the hotel search results page in React with server-side rendering, cutting median load time from 3.8s to 1.6s and raising bookings per search 9% in an A/B test.
Westfield State University | Web Developer, IT Services | Metro City, USA | Jul 2023 - Aug 2024
- Owned the department websites and the shared component library other developers relied on.
- Interviewed 8 department editors about publishing; the findings led to a preview mode that cut broken pages reported by students from 30 to 6 a month.
- Wrote the accessibility checklist for all university web pages, reducing failed audits from 12 to 2 a semester.
- Rebuilt the course-catalog search with client-side filtering, cutting search time from 4 seconds to under 1.
PROJECTS
Transit Arrival Web App | Independent Project | TypeScript, React | Oct 2025 - Present
- Built a progressive web app showing live bus arrivals for 400 stops, used by about 900 riders a week.
- Cached the stop list offline, so the app opened in 0.8s on a slow 3G connection against 2.9s before.
- Open-sourced the app, and the city transit agency linked it from its developer page.
Library Room Booking | Hackathon, Team of 4 | Vue | Feb 2024 - Mar 2024
- Worked on the frontend of the booking flow using React and TypeScript.
- Wrote the booking calendar component and its tests, handling overlapping bookings and time-zone changes.
- Rebuilt a travel search page with server rendering, more than halving its load time and lifting bookings by about a tenth.
SKILLS
Tools: TypeScript, React, Vue, Storybok, Angular
Methods: server-side rendering, accessibility, component testing

items.says: The unrelated Harbor Coffee Roasters role should not have two bullets at the front of the technical career story.
items.because: Its routine duties make it more prominent than the technical experience most relevant to a technical reader.

items.says: The review says “cafØ” is corrupted text and should be “café.”
items.because: The visible Ø makes the sentence look incorrect.

items.says: The 35% improvement has no named performance metric or baseline.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what the percentage measures or assess it.

items.says: The 14 resolved accessibility issues should lead the bullet.
The three caught regressions should be attached directly to the tests.
The stated LCP improvement is not plausibly caused by lazy-loading the hero image under ordinary conditions.
items.because: If the hero image was the LCP element, lazy-loading it would typically delay its request.

items.says: The LCP result should come before the implementation method.
Storing input in React state does not prevent XSS when it is rendered with dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
items.because: React state does not sanitize or escape user content, and raw HTML can still allow executable markup.

items.says: The XSS-prevention claim has no verification evidence.
items.because: Without a security check and result, a reader cannot assess whether prevention was verified.

items.says: The hotel-search result should lead the internship bullets.
items.because: Its load-time reduction and A/B-test booking result are strong evidence a reader should see early.

items.says: “Owned” does not name the work performed on the websites or component library.
items.because: A reader cannot picture the candidate’s concrete contribution or what improved.

items.says: “Other developers relied on” is an unnecessary qualifier for “shared component library.”
The reduction in broken-page reports should lead the bullet.
items.because: Putting the clearest evidence of impact first helps a scanning reader find it.

items.says: “The findings led to a preview mode” leaves the candidate’s role in creating the mode unclear.
The live-arrival bullet does not say how the arrival data reached the app.
items.because: Without the data source and integration detail, a reader cannot picture the technical contribution.

items.says: “Against 2.9s before” does not make clear what the baseline describes.
The booking-flow bullet names React while the project heading names Vue.
items.because: The conflicting frontend stacks make it unclear which technology was used.

items.says: The booking-flow bullet does not name the specific frontend work or what it enabled.
The calendar component should lead the project bullets.
items.because: It fits the project and makes its relevant work clear first.

items.says: “Its tests” does not say what the tests verified.
The travel-search result does not fit the library booking project and duplicates a result attributed to the Lumen internship.
items.because: The similar server-rendering, load-time and bookings claims make the attribution difficult to trust.

items.says: “Storybok” is misspelled; the correct spelling is “Storybook.”
items.because: The misspelling makes a named tool look incorrect.

items.says: Angular is listed without supporting experience or project evidence.
items.because: A reader cannot connect it to any described work in the résumé.
